notesStmt.note: Whitman was working on his "Old-Age Recitatives" cluster in late 1890, so this manuscript likely dates from mid-to-late 1890.

Early stage draft lines of a poem titled "This Journey." Whitman included the piece, retitled "My Task," in a cluster of poems that he had printed in proof sheets and submitted for publication in late 1890. The cluster was titled "Old-Age Recitatives" (see loc.00231 and loc.00232), but was seemingly never published in that form or under that title. This poem later was incorporated as lines 6, 7, 8, and 9 in "L. of G.'s Purport," first published in Good-Bye My Fancy in 1891.

lg.head: This journey
lg.l:
Begun in amid my ripen'd youth, and stretching steadily
kept on and on, thro' life
I end it ‸them here in old age.

Delaying, dallying, wandering,—never ‸even for a one day single hour brief day
abandon'd
